races.name: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's consistent sprinter returns after 18 days and carries Oisin Murphy, boasting a recent 5f win on Good and strong similar-going form (12/14); a natural prominent runner with the tactical speed to slot directly behind the pace-setters and likely to be fighting out the finish if the front trio fold.|
runners_data.comment: Dubai Bling arrives here on the back of a win two starts ago and boasts experience of both today's trip and going, and at 138 lb from stall 17 he brings solid claims with two wins in his last six starts; the main risk is a trainer operating at just 4% over the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: Palmer's second string for this race, Stratusnine has placed multiple times on Good ground over 5-6f and James Doyle will be positive from the gate; similar-going form reads well (8/15) but an OR of 104 sets a stiff task, and finishing second or third in recent starts hints at a horse that gets beat rather than wins.|
runners_data.comment: Stratusnine arrives in fine fettle after finishing second last time out, and a winner two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour. The trainer's recent strike rate is a mild concern, but the 18-day turnaround looks ideal and he merits respect off 138 lb from stall 16.

runners_data.name: West Acre
runners_data.note: George Scott's runner arrives fresh (18 days) and has boarded at 5f on Good before; Darragh Keenan takes the ride for a yard in reasonable form (T14: 3/12), but a last run of 19th over 6f on Good and a form string showing a 5 and 0 recently means confidence is not high that this trip draws out his best.|
runners_data.comment: West Acre is the top-rated runner in a field of 22 and shaped with promise when third two starts back, making him a leading danger off a workable 18-day break with distance experience to call on; the concern is that he steps back from an unplaced effort last time and remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for John & Sean Quinn, Dark Thirty has three wins on Good ground and a recent second over 6f in this going; Jason Hart will be patient and this six-year-old's ability to finish from off a fast pace makes it one of the more interesting profiles in a race where the early gallop should be fierce.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out tempers expectations, though Dark Thirty boasts a win three starts back and a runner-up finish two starts back, bringing genuine recent form to the table; experience over today's trip and going and a return after 18 days suggest he is ready to go, but 134 lb from stall 13 is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Corolla Point
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's yard is in strong form (T14: 9/23) and Corolla Point has two wins at 5f on Good, most recently placed twice over sprint trips; Callum Rodriguez will try to secure a handy pitch from stall, and if he can do so this horse has the profile to sustain a challenge as leaders weaken.|
runners_data.comment: Corolla Point arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 39% recently; 134 lb from stall nine is the query.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's confirmed front-runner will go straight to the lead under Edward Greatrex, but faces the problem of two other confirmed pace-setters likely to push for the same territory; a win over 5f Good is on the card, but burn-out is a real threat in a field this competitive for early position.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back give Lexington Blitz some credibility, but he was well beaten in sixth last time out and must bounce back off a 22-day break; has run over today's distance and going, and 132 lb from stall one is the challenge he faces.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: George Wood takes the ride on this hold-up type, who showed a best effort with a 6f Soft win but has run poorly twice since on Good ground (27th, 23rd); form figures of 416-00 suggest significant regression and the compressed midfield in this race makes a revival very hard to construct.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in each of his last two starts, Candy showed better when winning four starts back, but that dip in form is the concern; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 131 lb from stall 2 makes this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Against The Wind
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's front-runner is 97 days since last racing and ran 21st last time on Good, raising fitness questions despite the trainer's decent record; Kevin Stott will be committed to making the running, but coming off a long break against two fresh, confirmed pace rivals is a significant vulnerability.|
runners_data.comment: Against The Wind has a pair of thirds in recent starts but is winless in his last five, and a 97-day absence, a trainer among the winners at just 5% over the past fortnight, and a hefty 131 lb burden all give pause heading into this.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old has run all 15 of its recent starts on Good ground — an outstanding positional stat — and Daniel Tudhope is one of the shrewdest jockeys in this type of race; a hold-up horse with a single 5f Good win in recent form, Toca Madera's profile suits a race where front-runners go hard.|
runners_data.comment: Toca Madera won five starts back in his recent form but has since posted a sixth, an unplaced run, a fourth and a fifth, so consistency is the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 130 lb from stall four, and returns after 18 days off.

runners_data.name: Trefor
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' five-year-old was last seen winning over 6f on Good just nine days ago and carries confidence into this return; a genuine hold-up horse who has won four of 14 starts on Good, Trefor is the freshest of the closers and Kieran Shoemark will be watching the pace collapse ahead — the quick turnaround is worth monitoring but connections clearly have faith.|
runners_data.comment: Trefor has been unplaced in three of his last five starts, and his ranking of 18th of 22 on our figures makes him hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable weight of 130 lb; he does bring distance and going experience, and that win last time out at least confirms he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with tongue tie for D J Murphy, this horse has run 14 of 15 recent starts on Good ground and is thoroughly exposed at this level (no wins in recent form figures); runs from behind, will face a congested midfield, and needs a perfect passage that is rarely available in 22-runner sprint handicaps.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Erosandpsyche does at least bring strong recent form — second two starts back and third on two further occasions — though that eight-start back effort is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and 129 lb from stall eight is the weight to beat at a rating of 95.

runners_data.name: Naana's Sparkle
runners_data.note: Lemos De Souza's four-year-old carries a tongue tie and has wins at 5f on Good, with Kieran O'Neill booked for a yard that has been active lately (T14: 3/11); a prominent runner who should get a reasonable position, the horse's similar-going form of 10/15 and ability to front-up makes it a quiet each-way interest.|
runners_data.comment: Naana's Sparkle catches the eye with a second last time out and a winner two starts back, showing he retains ability, though a fourth three starts back and a sixth in recent starts are a reminder he can disappoint; experience over today's trip and going and 22 days since his last run suggest he arrives ready.

runners_data.name: Spartan Arrow
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's hold-up runner is equipped with a hood and has not finished better than seventh in any of its last six starts; similar-going figures of 9/15 don't inspire and Luke Morris will need a bunched finish and perfect routing through traffic — the form string 788077 says this horse is struggling at current handicap level.|
runners_data.comment: Spartan Arrow is yet to score in his last six starts, with a run of seventh, seventh, and eighth positions making grim reading, and his trainer is winless from 22 attempts in the past fortnight; he has run over today's trip and going, but that experience alone offers limited encouragement here.

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's four-year-old has won three of its last six starts, including two on Soft/Standard, and Hector Crouch rides for a yard returning a winner recently (T14: 1/18); equipped with a hood, this confirmed front-runner will jump and try to steal a march, but it has no recorded win on Good ground in the last five starts and faces two fresh rivals fighting for the same position.|
runners_data.comment: Gold Star Hero has run over today's trip and going, and finished second last time out after an unplaced effort two starts back, but ranked 19th of 22 on our figures he faces a stiff ask at the weights, and that patchy recent consistency makes him hard to fancy despite his three wins in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old has been off 60 days and ran 19th last time on Good, with only one win in similar going across 15 recent runs; Rossa Ryan takes the ride but the layoff combined with poor recent turf form and a form string showing 6f biases make the 5½f trip at York a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked a long way down the field on our figures, Toyotomi faces a stiff task from stall 21, and an unplaced effort last time out on a 60-day break does little to inspire confidence, though he has winning form two starts back and experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran for a small yard, Apollo One has run nine times recently on Good ground without a win, and Colin Keane cannot disguise what the form figures say; placed once at OR 91 level over 6f on Good, but consistent double-digit finishes make it very hard to construct a winning scenario at this competitive level.|
runners_data.comment: Apollo One arrives here freshened by a 25-day break, has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 106 ranks him second of 22 runners, suggesting he merits serious respect; the worry is that he has been winless in recent starts, with two unplaced efforts immediately preceding this.

runners_data.name: Dapper Valley
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides for Michael Keady, who has not had a 14-day winner recently; this horse is a genuine hold-up type by style but has been redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with closers — its most recent wins came at 5-6f on Good and it has strong form credentials, but racing somewhat out of its natural slot tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and a lengthy 108 days absent, Dapper Valley is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but the fitness query is real from stall 15 off 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: Geoff Oldroyd's five-year-old is fitted with a visor and P J McDonald takes the ride; a natural hold-up horse by style, it finds itself pushed into a midfield position on the map because the true rear is overcrowded, and while it has placed five times on Good ground, winning from a compromised position in a 22-runner sprint is a difficult task.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Air Force One faces a stiff task against 21 rivals, and a single win in his last six starts does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's distance and going before and arrives here on a reasonable 25-day break.

runners_data.name: Stormy Impact
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (claimer, 3lb) partners this Richard & Peter Fahey four-year-old, a yard in strong form (T14: 5/31); a genuine hold-up type that has been shifted into a midfield role due to field congestion at the rear, its form string of 6-0450 and mixed similar-going stats (10/15) suggest it is below the level required to win here even from its natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Stormy Impact has at least shown some consistency through a pair of midfield finishes, though the unplaced efforts either side temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and going before and the weight of 123 lb from stall 11 makes her a watch-and-see proposition.

runners_data.name: The Man
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's four-year-old carries a tongue-and-palate bar and has run six consecutive times without finishing in the top five on Good-or-similar ground; David Egan takes the ride but the form string -66600 is brutal for a 22-runner handicap, and this horse — a natural hold-up type packed into a midfield slot — faces a near-impossible task.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Man nevertheless carries an encouraging 10 lb pull between his official mark and our rating, suggesting he remains capable of better; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 22 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to do himself justice from stall three.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old ran just four days ago and is a bold repeat runner, equipped with a hood; a hold-up horse in style but squeezed into a midfield slot on the map, it did win over 5f on Good last time out but the very quick turnaround and the sheer pace of this race make a repeat performance extremely unlikely.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Ziggy's Triton has been unplaced in two of his most recent starts and faces a stiff task from stall 14 off 122 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and showed he retains ability with a win three starts back.

runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's six-
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 21 of 22 on our figures, Another Baar makes a tough case to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after just 18 days, suggesting he is fit and ready.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Blitz, Against The Wind, and Gold Star Hero are all confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field over 5½f at York, making a fierce early gallop a near-certainty from the gates — these three will fight for supremacy up front and are unlikely to all get clean air, burning fuel at a rate that will test their stamina reserves significantly. The pace is so strong that prominent types Dubai Bling, Stratusnine, Corolla Point, and West Acre will also be pressing hard in the first two furlongs, compressing the entire front half of the field and leaving nowhere to hide. With the race shape set to produce a genuine end-to-end gallop on Good turf at York — a track that already rewards those who travel well through a race — stamina and the ability to sustain a finish from midfield will be at a premium. This race shape firmly favours horses who can race in midfield or just off a hot pace and pick up when the leaders tie each other up, making genuine mid-division runners with tactical speed and proven Good-ground form the most dangerous profiles. Several runners tagged as hold-up types — including Dapper Valley, Air Force One, The Man, Stormy Impact, Ziggy's Triton, Another Baar, and Ziggy's Triton — are mapped to midfield because the field's true rear is saturated; those most likely to secure a genuine prominent position ahead of them are Dubai Bling and Corolla Point, who have the tactical pace to slot in naturally.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out through a blistering first half, leaving midfield horses to sprint past exhausted leaders.
scenarios.body: Lexington Blitz, Against The Wind, and Gold Star Hero set a punishing gallop that leaves them vulnerable in the final furlong, opening the race wide for those tracking just off the pace from the middle of the field; Toca Madera, Dark Thirty, and Trefor — all proven on Good ground and comfortable settling — are ideally positioned to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking the pace in second or third position conserves enough energy to sustain a strong finish as front-runners weaken.
scenarios.body: Dubai Bling or Corolla Point, armed with the tactical speed to sit just off the early leaders, are best placed to benefit as the pace-setters begin to tie up; both have solid Good-ground form at sprint trips and their jockeys — Murphy and Rodriguez — are well capable of timing the move to perfection.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed front-runners — most likely Gold Star Hero or Lexington Blitz — breaks cleanly and secures a clear lead while rivals check each other in a three-way battle for supremacy.
scenarios.body: Should one front-runner get a soft lead while the others bump or check early, that horse could control the tempo and steal a march on the field; Gold Star Hero's recent winning form and course familiarity makes it the most credible beneficiary of such a scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of multiple hold-up types allows one genuine closer to weave through an unusually congested midfield and unleash a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario is dampened by the reality that most of the horses who would thrive coming from furthest back — Dapper Valley, Air Force One, The Man — are not in their natural position and must navigate a compressed midfield; only Trefor and Erosandpsyche, the most genuine hold-up types in the field, could realistically find a clear run late enough to matter.

races.name: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's hold-up performer has two wins over 7f on Good going in his last five runs and arrives fresh at 26 days; his proven stamina and late-running style make this pace-heavy scenario his most natural hunting ground, and Kieran Shoemark has ridden him to both course-distance victories.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him obvious claims, but he was fifth two starts back and has been inconsistent in recent starts; 129 lb from stall eight adds to the query marks against a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's prominent runner has won over 6f on Good and arrives 20 days since his last run; stepping up to 7f for the first time is the primary concern here, and while he handles Good ground well, the question is whether he will see out the extra furlong in a gruelling pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Big Cigar won two starts back and has run over today's trip, and at 129 lb he carries plenty, which is the main thing to overcome.

runners_data.name: Clash Of Hearts
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's front-runner carries the lowest OR in the field at 83 and is stepping into Group 3 company for the first time; he won over 6f on Good but faces a significant class rise, and with multiple stronger pace-setters drawn against him, securing a prominent position will be difficult — likely to be swallowed up early.
runners_data.comment: Clash Of Hearts won two starts back but has since dropped to eighth, so he arrives with mixed signals; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 129 lb from stall five, and our rating of 95 suggests potential, though that latest effort leaves something to prove.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's prominent racer has been consistent at 6f on Good but is stepping up in trip for the first time, and three consecutive thirds suggest he may be finding his level; Wayne Lordan picks up the ride, and if the pace burns out the leaders he has the tactical nous to arrive at the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Confucius has placed in each of his last two starts and was a winner four starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going to call on; carrying 129 lb from stall 10, his rating of 106 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Fuel The Jet
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's front-runner is rated 120 and won over this exact 7f Good combination last time out, with Neil Callan booked; his two-run form is limited but both efforts are over this trip and surface, and he is one of the more credible pace-setters who could sustain his effort if he escapes the early scramble with a clean lead.
runners_data.comment: Useful to note he won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked ninth of eleven on our figures and a speed rating of 70 makes him hard to fancy at the weights, carrying 129 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Gentle Hurricane
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's prominent filly is unbeaten in one run over 6f on Good but steps up sharply in trip and class; Oisin Murphy's booking is significant, and her single impressive win suggests raw quality — the 7f trip is an unknown but her prominent style should allow her to race within herself before challenging.
runners_data.comment: Gentle Hurricane won last time out, but our figures rank him tenth of eleven in this field, and with a speed rating of 67 he has plenty to find; experience over today's trip offers some hope, yet it is hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Haffner
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount is trained by Aidan O'Brien, has placed twice at 7f on Good and won over this trip, and is the highest-profile lead contender with legitimate credentials; Moore may attempt to control the pace rather than burn him out in the early battle, but with five other front-runners he will face significant early pressure regardless.
runners_data.comment: Haffner arrives here just 22 days since a runner-up effort, backed by a runner-up last time out and consistency throughout recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, and the main query is whether 129 lb from stall 11 blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Siouxperb
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's front-runner won over 6f on Good but his trainer has zero winners in the last 14 days and he finished 18th last time out on Good ground before bouncing back; the step up to 7f in a Group 3 with this many pace horses is a big ask, and Hector Crouch will struggle to find clear air early.
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out and a winner three starts back, Siouxperb has distance experience to call on and comes here on a quick enough turnaround at 19 days, though an unplaced effort two starts back and a rating of 84 leave him with something to prove from stall two carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Stardom Glory
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's prominent type has placed twice and won over 6f on Good, but 53 days since his last run is the longest absence in the field; James Doyle takes the ride and the step to 7f from 6f winners' form is not a guaranteed fit, though his positioning just off the pace could allow him to avoid the worst of the front-runner carnage.
runners_data.comment: Ran well in his last three starts — a winner most recently and a runner-up two starts back — but 53 days off the track and carrying 129 lb from stall 4 are the checks, though he does hold experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Trean
runners_data.note: Paul Twomey's front-runner is rated 120 and won over 7f on Good last time out, but his 10th on his previous attempt over 6f is a flag; he wears headgear and arrives 23 days fresh, but with WJ Lee riding in a race packed with rival pace horses, he cannot expect to lead uncontested and his stamina may be stretched in a contested pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Trean won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, giving him a solid platform from stall seven carrying 129 lb; the unplaced effort two starts back is the one nagging doubt.

runners_data.name: Vega King
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's front-runner has won over a mile on Good and finished fourth over 7f on Good, suggesting the trip suits and he may actually be the most naturally suited to the distance among the pace setters; Clifford Lee rides, and while his OR of 92 means he is outrated by the top three, if the pace is moderate he could outrun his mark.
runners_data.comment: Vega King won last time out but our rating puts him well below the top-ranked runners in this field, and he has to carry 129 lb from stall 3; experience over today's trip offers some encouragement, but he looks to have plenty to find on these figures.

races.paceDynamic: Trean, Fuel The Jet, Haffner, Clash Of Hearts, Siouxperb, and Vega King all carry front-running profiles, guaranteeing a fierce early battle for supremacy over York's straight 7f on Good ground. With six horses seeking the lead, the opening two furlongs will be intensely contested, meaning no single horse is likely to dictate uncontested, and the collective early pace will be fierce enough to test stamina significantly by the final two furlongs. Fuel The Jet and Haffner are the highest-rated of the speed brigade and likely to press hardest into the early lead, but even they will face pressure from Trean on the outside. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses with class and stamina — runners like Alfred Wallace and Gentle Hurricane, who can let the pace-setters burn each other out and arrive with a sustained late run, are the primary beneficiaries of this scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the six front-runners fight for supremacy and collectively set a strong enough pace to exhaust each other in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The early scramble drains Fuel The Jet, Haffner, and Trean of their finishing reserves, leaving the race wide open for hold-up horses to sweep past the fading leaders; Alfred Wallace, proven at 7f on Good and an effective closer, is ideally positioned to deliver a late challenge, while Gentle Hurricane's class gives her the power to reel in tiring rivals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Escapes Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Fuel The Jet or Haffner manages to establish a decisive early advantage and dictates at a controlled but strong gallop rather than a chaotic scramble.
scenarios.body: One of the top-rated pace setters slips the field by half a length or more going into the first two furlongs and, with the others unable to match the early stride-for-stride pressure, sets a rhythm that suits a horse with tactical speed and class; Fuel The Jet, rated 120 and a winner over this course and distance, is most capable of sustaining a front-running effort to the line under a confident Neil Callan ride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not destructive, and one of the higher-class prominent runners tracks the leaders effectively before producing a decisive finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Confucius or Stardom Glory, sitting just off the hot pace from their prominent positions, avoid the early scrimmage and have enough left to close powerfully in the final furlong; this shape requires the pace to be fast but not utterly brutal, keeping the prominent horses competitive without exhausting them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runners Survive
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple front-runners check each other early but then collectively settle into a moderate gallop, negating the anticipated pace war.
scenarios.body: Should the jockeys on Trean, Fuel The Jet, and Haffner collectively ease off after the initial skirmish, the race becomes a sprint-style dash in the final two furlongs where tactical speed is rewarded over stamina; in that scenario, a front-runner like Vega King who has won over a mile on Good ground and can sustain his effort may outlast those who were expected to tire.

watchPoints.text: With Trean, Fuel The Jet, Haffner, Clash Of Hearts, Siouxperb, and Vega King all seeking the lead, watch the first two furlongs for a genuine pace war — if they burn each other out, hold-up runners Alfred Wallace and Gentle Hurricane become prime dangers in the final furlong.

Fuel The Jet (OR 120, won over 7f Good) and Haffner (OR 108, Ryan Moore) are the two pace setters with the best chance of sustaining a front-running effort — if either establishes a clear advantage after 2f, they become very hard to run down.

Gentle Hurricane is unbeaten but has only one career run over 6f — her stamina for 7f in a strongly-run Group 3 is completely unproven and Oisin Murphy will need to manage her carefully to avoid her stopping in the final furlong.

Alfred Wallace has the most relevant winning form in the race (two wins at 7f Good) and is freshened at 26 days — watch how Kieran Shoemark positions him early; if he gets a clean passage through mid-pack he is the textbook profile for this pace scenario.

Confucius has posted three consecutive thirds for O'Brien and makes his first start at 7f — watch his market moves, as stable confidence from Wayne Lordan's booking and a trip that should suit his stamina profile could mean he is underrated despite the uninspiring recent form string.

races.name: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Christmas Day
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's leading light over this trip, Ryan Moore takes the ride and the form figures of 1-1 underline class; sits naturally prominent and Good ground has yielded six places from eight comparable runs — well-placed to pounce if Antigua's lead is retrievable.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and battle-hardened, Christmas Day has won three times in his last five starts, with a victory two starts back sandwiched by a second last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going. The 52-day absence is the only query.

runners_data.name: Maltese Cross
runners_data.note: William Haggas has been in excellent form (6/39 over 14 days) and Maltese Cross owns a strong record at 1m2f-1m4f on Good; though shown at the rear here, this is a horse that genuinely wants to race prominently and will try to travel closer than the map suggests — the repositioning is situational rather than tactical.
runners_data.comment: Maltese Cross arrives on the back of four wins in his last five starts, with a runner-up finish two starts back the only blot on a sparkling recent record, and he has experience of today's distance and going. The 36-day absence is the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Antigua
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shape architect; OR of 87 flatters the situation — her role is to control fractions, not to win, though a very slow pace could allow her to exploit a sleeping field as she did over 1m2f at York (won, LR 52d); tongue-tie fitted.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and unplaced last time, Antigua faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a victory two starts back shows he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Galiyan
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners a horse whose natural instinct is to race in the first half of the field, but with four prominent horses in a six-runner field, he is inevitably pushed wider and deeper; one win from four on Good and a recent sixth at 1m6f Goodwood tempers enthusiasm, though his course win at 1m2f here is relevant.
runners_data.comment: Galiyan shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out, and he was a winner three starts back, bringing solid recent form into this; he has run over today's trip and going, and 107-rated, he looks a genuine danger, though 41 days off the track is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Pierre Bonnard
runners_data.note: A versatile O'Brien runner with a record that includes a course win and strong placed efforts at 1m2f-1m4f on Good; drops back from a seventh at Leopardstown but the form either side of that run is more encouraging — a natural sit-and-kick pattern suits a race run like this.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a runner-up three starts back, Pierre Bonnard arrives with solid recent form and handles today's distance and going, while our rating of 124 marks him as a genuine threat off 128 lb; the main risk is a 52-day absence since that encouraging effort.

runners_data.name: Superior Choice
runners_data.note: Three wins from three on Good ground and a rapid rise through the ranks for Gosden; however, like Galiyan, this horse naturally wants to be on the pace and being shuffled to midfield in a small field means he races against his instincts — the unbeaten Good-ground record is compelling but the positional compromise is real.
runners_data.comment: Superior Choice arrives on the back of three consecutive wins, which is the obvious headline, but our rating of 101 ranks him fifth of six in this field, and a speed figure of 80 suggests the level of those victories may fall short of what is required here.

races.paceDynamic: Antigua is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just six runners on Good ground over 1m4f at York, is virtually certain to lead from the outset — the question is not whether she sets the pace but how sustainable and unchallenged that lead becomes. Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard are genuine prominent types who will press forward behind her, meaning Antigua is unlikely to be left entirely alone, but neither is likely to pressure her aggressively enough to turn this into a true test of stamina from the front. This creates a controlled, single-file rhythm that will compress the field and make it extremely difficult for anything to manufacture a meaningful gap in the straight — the race is likely to be decided by a sharp turn of foot in the final two furlongs, favouring prominent racers with a quality sprint rather than deep closers. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all occupy that position: Galiyan and Superior Choice are both natural prominent racers who will be shuffled back into a midfield role they do not naturally seek, meaning the true prominent berths behind Antigua will be claimed by Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Antigua sets a fair but unchallenged gallop and the race becomes a sprint for home from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Antigua bowls along in front at a measured clip, with Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard tracking in a compact group; the tempo remains honest rather than punishing, and the race ignites late when the field quickens together.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Antigua Stolen Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so sedate that Antigua builds an unassailable lead before the field realises the danger.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to commit to chasing her down early, Antigua extends her advantage into the straight and the prominent horses behind run into each other's pockets, leaving her untouchable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Unravels Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Pierre Bonnard or Christmas Day pushes forward to pressurise Antigua and the tempo becomes genuinely strong.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace stretches the field and suits those with proven stamina at 1m4f and beyond; any horse that has won over further or shown relentless galloping ability benefits from the race not becoming a sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to stop the leaders and the redistributed prominent horses have settled deeply enough to deliver a late run.
scenarios.body: Galiyan or Superior Choice, racing out of their preferred position, would need the front group to tie up in the final furlong and produce a strong sustained finish — a low-probability shape given neither is a natural hold-up horse.

watchPoints.text: Antigua's early fractions will define everything — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged through the first half-mile, the prominent horses behind Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard face a tactical dilemma that could leave the back half of the field with far too much to do.

Galiyan and Superior Choice are both prominent types forced into midfield; watch for either horse attempting to recover its natural position early, which could create unexpected pressure on Antigua before the race settles.

Christmas Day is 52 days since last run and A P O'Brien's 14-day strike rate of 9/35 is solid rather than exceptional — a fitness or freshness caveat exists for Ryan Moore's mount despite the strong form figures.

Maltese Cross's redistribution to the rear is situational; Tom Marquand is likely to push forward from the break to reclaim a prominent pitch, meaning the actual race shape may be more compressed than the map indicates with five horses in a tight bunch behind Antigua.

races.name: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almaqam
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old confirmed front-runner with nine wins from 13 on similar going; has every right to fight for the lead from the off, and his record over 10f on good ground (three wins, seven places) is solid, though he faces stiffer Grade-1 company here than in recent wins.
runners_data.comment: Almaqam brings strong claims on the back of a win two starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the concern is a return from 63 days off carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Devil's Advocate
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has yet to win at Group 1 level and whose record in top-level fields (0W0P from 11 similar-going runs) is the notable concern; headgear flag noted, and Havlin will need a clean passage late if this shape develops into a strong-pace scenario that suits closers.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and returning after 63 days off, Devil's Advocate is hard to fancy on recent form that shows three finishes of fourth or worse in his last four starts, though he has a win five starts back and experience over today's trip and going in his favour.

runners_data.name: Ombudsman
runners_data.note: William Buick partners the form horse of the race — five wins from his last five, 10 wins from 12 on good ground, and an outstanding stats profile for both jockey and trainer over the past fortnight; settled prominent style ideally maps to the anticipated race shape here.
runners_data.comment: Ombudsman arrives on the back of three consecutive wins and has won four of his last five starts, giving him a compelling recent profile, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the 63-day absence is the one query, but his class speaks loudly.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won over 1m2f on good ground 25 days ago and is therefore fresh; his good-ground record (3W4P from 8 runs) is respectable, but a Group 1 jump in class on a compressed preparation makes the ask steep, even if the pace scenario plays into his hands.
runners_data.comment: Pride Of Arras showed well when second last time out, and a winner four starts back, but the eighth two starts back is harder to ignore; carrying 134 lb from stall five, he has experience over today's trip and going, and returns on a workable 25-day break.

runners_data.name: Zaydann
runners_data.note: Unbeaten five-timer for Graffard, all victories on softer ground or synthetic surfaces; stepping up sharply in class and trip-type on fast good going is the central question, though his prominent style and ability to travel efficiently make him dangerous if he handles the surface change.
runners_data.comment: Zaydann has won each of his last five starts and arrives here 28 days fresh, carrying 134 lb from stall nine; still unexposed, there could be more to come from a colt who continues to answer every question put to him.

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's three-year-old whose best recent form is a Group 2 second on good ground; a genuine prominent type whose natural position is overfilled in this field, meaning Ronan Whelan will likely find him further back than ideal — the style fit discount is real and his recent form tailing off (sixth, seventh, 12th in last three) adds to the concern.
runners_data.comment: Action is winless in his last five starts, though a second four starts back offers some encouragement; fitness looks fine at 25 days since his last run and he has distance and going experience to call on, but recent form has been modest.

runners_data.name: Constitution River
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on an unbeaten five-from-five prospect who has won every start on good ground; the key tactical question is whether he can find a clean lead or whether Almaqam forces a genuine fight — if Moore can control the fractions, the record demands respect.
runners_data.comment: Constitution River arrives in blistering form with five consecutive wins in his last five starts, and he has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; carrying 127 lb from stall seven is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Hawk Mountain
runners_data.note: Prominent type with headgear noted, Wayne Lordan booked for O'Brien's second string; three-year-old whose last three starts have been placed rather than winning, suggesting he's slightly below the top level here, though a fluent passage from a tracking position gives him an each-way avenue.
runners_data.comment: Hawk Mountain arrives with three wins in his last five starts, including a victory three starts back, and has experience of today's trip and going — the 46-day absence is the one question mark over his readiness.

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners Andrew Balding's three-year-old who has won three of his last five on good ground; comfortable in prominent positions and his York form profile on this surface (3W from 3 comparable runs) is the headline positive, making him one to respect if he avoids the prominent-position scrum.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below his official mark on our figures and ranked seventh of nine, Item faces a stiff ask, though four wins in his last five starts — including a win last time out — and experience over today's trip and going offer genuine positives from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Constitution River and Almaqam will both want to lead, setting up a genuinely contested early pace over this 1m2½f trip on good ground at York — neither is likely to concede without a fight, so the gallop from the off should be honest rather than dawdling. Ombudsman, Zaydann, Hawk Mountain, and Item all want prominent positions, creating a congested group of five runners chasing the first two or three slots, which raises a real traffic danger between two and three furlongs out as the field compresses into the straight. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position; Constitution River and Almaqam are best placed to actually lead, with Ombudsman likeliest to slot in just behind, while Action is a genuine prominent runner redistributed to midfield in this map because the position is already overfilled. A contested pace on quick good ground at York over this trip historically produces a race where the prominent-to-midfield stalker who travels fluently and quickens in the last quarter-mile profits most — horses who press from a handy pitch without burning energy in the early jostle are the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Constitution River and Almaqam set a genuine contested gallop that stretches the field and the prominent stalkers inherit a well-run race.
scenarios.body: The honest early duel between Constitution River and Almaqam ensures no favours are granted up front, and runners who settle just off the pace conserve energy for a meaningful finish through the York straight; Ombudsman, with five wins from his last five and a near-perfect record on good ground, is ideally placed to dictate from a prominent pitch and pick off the leaders. Zaydann's unbeaten sequence and Item's strong form also suit this shape, both capable of tracking efficiently and unleashing a clean turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Soften, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the front two push each other hard enough early that they tie each other up, leaving room for hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Constitution River and Almaqam's duel becomes a war of attrition, and the pair's declining momentum in the final two furlongs opens a gap for horses coming from further back; Pride Of Arras, who won over 1m2f on good ground and relishes this trip, is the natural beneficiary, as is Devil's Advocate if he can find clear running. The scenario is plausible but depends on a degree of early overexertion that honest rather than reckless pace may not produce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Constitution River Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Constitution River establishes a smooth, uncontested lead by finding a comfortable rhythm that Almaqam cannot or does not press vigorously.
scenarios.body: Ryan Moore's positive front-running tactics could allow Constitution River to dictate a controlled gallop, conserving energy while the field behind tangles for prominent positions; Constitution River's six-from-six record on good ground and class at the top level make this a dangerous scenario to overlook if the pace becomes his to manage. Ombudsman pressing efficiently could also slot into a pace-following role here, but the leader gains the largest advantage if the gallop is truly measured.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion two to three furlongs out causes interference or checks, scrambling the market order.
scenarios.body: With four or five horses fighting for prominent ground and Action squeezed out of a natural position, a moment of crowding in the straight could stop fancied runners cold and hand a clean run to one who finds daylight; Hawk Mountain, who has won in smaller fields and handles fast good ground, could benefit if he threads through, and Pride Of Arras also retains an each-way angle if traffic disrupts those ahead. This scenario requires a specific incident and is markedly discounted but is not negligible given the documented prominent congestion.

watchPoints.text: Constitution River and Almaqam will both load wanting to lead — watch the first furlong closely to see whether Almaqam applies genuine pressure or drops off early, as this determines whether the pace is truly contested or slides into Moore's hands.

Prominent congestion involving Ombudsman, Zaydann, Hawk Mountain, Item, and Action creates a compressed group of five chasing two or three spots; any checking or bumping between two and three furlongs out could derail even the best-placed horse in this section.

Action has been redistributed to midfield in this map but is a natural prominent type — watch whether Ronan Whelan attempts to push forward regardless, which could intensify early crowding and heighten traffic risk for those around him.

Zaydann's entire five-race unbeaten record was compiled on soft or synthetic ground; monitor his movement in the market on race morning as a proxy for stable confidence that he will handle fast good going at York.

Devil's Advocate and Pride Of Arras are the only true hold-up runners in a field that otherwise clusters towards the front — both need the honest pace to materialise and a clean run through traffic; if either is baulked two furlongs out, their chance evaporates quickly.

races.name: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Michael Bell who has run over today's trip before but his last five form figures include several disappointing efforts and he has no wins or places on similar Good ground in five attempts — needs a truly run race to produce his best late surge.|
runners_data.comment: Duke of Oxford brings a win in his recent form and has experience over today's distance and going, with a rating of 108 placing him second of 17 in this field; the concern is that he has finished 5th, 7th, 6th and unplaced since that victory.

runners_data.name: Prydwen
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes over on this 8-year-old who won at 12f last time on Good and has placed at 16f on Soft, but his Good-ground record over staying trips reads a single win from eight — the Gosden-style patient hold-up suits a well-run race.|
runners_data.comment: Prydwen shaped well when winning three starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a clear form pick at the top of the weights on 138 lb; the 53-day absence is the one query, but his rating of 108 marks him out as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Kirchner
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore is the key angle here — this 4-year-old won at 16f on Good and placed at 16f on Soft with proven prominent-racing style, and the big-race jockey booking plus a trainer firing at 9/40 over 14 days makes him hard to ignore in a position he should actually get.|
runners_data.comment: Kirchner arrives on the back of a win last time out and was second two starts back, giving him solid recent momentum, though a fifth three starts back and a seventh four starts back suggest some inconsistency; having run over today's trip before, he shapes as a genuine each-way player at 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Small Fry
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides for Joseph O'Brien on this 5-year-old who placed at 14f and 16f on Good this season — he is a genuine prominent type who should get his position early, but a career-high trip of 20f on Good saw him finish sixth, meaning stamina over 2m½f is a live question.|
runners_data.comment: Second last time out is his chief calling card, though sixth and ninth in the two starts before that highlight his inconsistency; has run over today's trip and going, carries a stiff 132 lb, but 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough to make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: William Buick partners this progressive 4-year-old who has won twice at 14f on Good and placed at 16f on Good, giving him the best recent Good-ground form in the field at these distances — headgear (blinkers) applied, prominent-style suits today's race shape, and the Gosden yard is in form at 4/16.|
runners_data.comment: Valedictory won back-to-back two and three starts back, so the winning thread is there, but a fifth last time out checks enthusiasm; he has experience of today's going and comes back quickly enough at 18 days, though 131 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Mordor
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer on Gordon Elliott's 6-year-old who won at 14f on Heavy and placed at 24f and 16f on Good — 64 days off the track is a concern, but Spencer is an expert at conserving energy in prominent positions and the further the trip the better this horse goes.|
runners_data.comment: Mordor showed his quality with a win three starts back and was third two starts back, but has been unplaced on his most recent outing and returns after a 64-day absence; he has experience of today's distance and going, though 130 lb is a stern enough burden for a runner ranked mid-field on ratings.

runners_data.name: Team Player
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old with two wins over 14-16f on Soft and Standard who finds Good going an open question based on his flat record at 8/15 in similar conditions — headgear (tongue strap and pads) worn, and Greg Fairley is an honest northern jockey, but the softer the ground the better his form has looked.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Team Player makes it hard to build a case, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table and returns from a 32-day break showing a recent second to his name.

runners_data.name: Manxman
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this 6-year-old who won at 16f on Good and placed at 16f on Soft, but he has not run for 351 days, which is the most significant flag in the field — the visor goes on, and the Crisford yard is hot at 10/26 over 14 days, yet that layoff over this trip demands caution.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win and a second in recent starts but has been unplaced twice since, and a lengthy absence of 351 days is a real concern; has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 38% offers some encouragement, but the rust may tell.

runners_data.name: In The Breeze
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides for Henrietta Knight on this 8-year-old who won at 12f on Soft and Good last time out — the trainer has only had two runners in 14 days, and a 73-day absence plus a poor record at 16f on Soft and Standard makes this a significant step up in both class and distance.|
runners_data.comment: In The Breeze has won twice in his last five starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of today's distance and going, but 73 days off the track raises a fitness query and 129 lb tests his resolve.

runners_data.name: Boatswain
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez's mount won at 16f on Standard and placed at 12f on Soft; at his core a front-running-to-prominent horse who has been pushed back on the map — in a field this congested with pace, he is unlikely to get anywhere near his natural berth, which significantly compromises how he performs.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 17 on our figures with a speed rating of 86, Boatswain is hard to fancy despite winning last time out, as the form either side of that success — a seventh and third in his two preceding starts, and more moderate efforts before that — suggests inconsistency; the trainer's 38% strike rate and experience over today's trip and going are the sole reasons for mild optimism.

runners_data.name: Westminster Moon
runners_data.note: Robbie Colgan and A.J. Martin team up on this 6-year-old who won at 14f on Good last time — a hold-up type who finished 13th over 17f and 20f on Good suggests stamina over 2m½f could be stretched, and the trainer has no runners placed from three attempts over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Westminster Moon won three starts back but has been unplaced in both runs since, and ranked 14 of 17 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; the fact he has run over today's trip and going at least brings some familiarity to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 4-year-old has a strong recent record — three wins and four places from 13 runs on similar going — but the high-traffic environment means this horse, a natural prominent type by inclination, is likely to find herself racing further back than ideal, constraining what has been a sharp, front-foot style.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Shrimp Shady faces a stiff ask at these weights, yet his recent form reads well with three wins in his last six starts, a runner-up finish last time out, and he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Kilmeaden
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this 4-year-old for Faye Bramley, who placed at 14f on Good and 16f on Good and Soft — a genuine wanting-to-be-prominent profile hemmed back by congestion; with a visor on and 11 days between runs, getting shuffled into midfield against her nature is a real tactical risk.|
runners_data.comment: Kilmeaden shaped with promise when third three starts back and runner-up five starts back, and he returns on a quick 11-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going — though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find more to bridge that gap.

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan's mount for Charlie Johnston is the lone confirmed front-runner and should lead from the outset at a sustainable tempo; an excellent Good-ground record at 12/15 in similar conditions is offset by the fact her form figures include multiple placings without winning, and at 2m½f her stamina is untested at this extreme trip.|
runners_data.comment: Ghaiyya shaped well when second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but sixth and eighth in the two starts before that give reason for caution; carrying 126 lb against a competitive field, she appeals as one likely to run her race without necessarily dominating.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark partners this 5-year-old for Dylan Cunha who has placed at 14f and 16f on Good — a horse that wants to race prominently but at 13/15 in similar-going form figures, his Good-ground conversion is the worst in the field; bumped back in the draw means a compromised run is the most likely outcome.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently competitive without quite getting his head in front, Fireblade arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second two starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before, though winless in his last five starts remains the sticking point under 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Ride The Thunder
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 4-year-old with Ray Dawson placed three times at 13-16f on Good and has a clean, honest record — a horse that naturally wants to press the pace but will be drawn into midfield by the congestion; the Varian yard is active at 6/22 and this horse's consistency could make it a factor if gaps appear.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent threat who has finished third or better in three of his last five starts, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; a trainer firing at 27% over the past fortnight adds significant support, though he remains yet to score and that final winning move is still the question mark.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Lauren Young's 5-pound claim helps Jim Goldie's 7-year-old on a low weight — won at 16f and placed at 13f and 16f on Good earlier in the season, making him one of the most proven in similar conditions; by nature a pressing, prominent horse who will be stuck further back than he wants, but the claimer and the course form are genuine positives.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Mountain Road is hard to fancy despite being lightly fit at 11 days between runs; he has run over today's trip and going, and was a winner two starts back, but his overall profile makes him a very difficult proposition here.

races.paceDynamic: Ghaiyya is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, with no natural challenger for the lead, is almost certain to bowl along at her own pace from the front — this sets up a controlled, single-file tempo over 2m½f on good ground at York, where the race will be run at a measured gallop and the real race will ignite turning for home. Seven horses — Kirchner, Small Fry, Valedictory, Mordor, Team Player, Manxman and In The Breeze — are all natural prominent-position horses, creating significant early positional congestion behind Ghaiyya from the two-mile chute, with traffic danger materialising two to three furlongs out as that group compresses around the home turn. The field holds more prominent types than can genuinely occupy the front rank: Boatswain, Shrimp Shady, Kilmeaden, Fireblade, Ride The Thunder and Mountain Road are all true prominent horses redistributed to midfield because the race shape simply cannot accommodate them, meaning they will need to find room on a track where the gaps can take time to appear. A steady-to-moderate pace with a sustained finish on good ground at this marathon trip — where stamina is the currency and tactical positioning matters enormously — strongly favours class hold-up and genuine stay-all-day horses who can track the late surge once the pack spreads, giving a structural edge to confirmed stayers with proven Good-ground form who can wait for the field to open up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghaiyya Controls, Stamina Settles
scenarios.trigger: If Ghaiyya leads uncontested at a fair clip and the race becomes a true test of staying at the death.
scenarios.body: Ghaiyya dictates from the front on her own terms, the field files behind and the race becomes a stamina examination from two furlongs out on the long York home straight; horses with proven staying credentials and Good-ground form who can travel smoothly in midfield before producing sustained runs are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ghaiyya dawdles and the pace is falsely slow, compressing the field and causing a sprint-like finish off the turn.
scenarios.body: With such a large group of natural prominent horses jostling behind a slow pace, the race will bunch dangerously off the home turn and whoever secures a clean early position two off the rail will fire first; prominent-placed horses who can quicken sharply in the straight on Good ground hold the advantage over hold-up types trapped in traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack goes hard early fighting for position, setting a genuine gallop that burns off the front rank.
scenarios.body: Sustained pace from multiple prominent horses taking each other on creates a truly run race over this marathon trip, leaving the front group spent and opening a fast lane up the outside for confirmed hold-up horses who can produce late, sweeping runs; the stamina-laden closers who have been patient throughout profit from a strung-out field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a redistibuted prominent horse like Shrimp Shady or Mountain Road forces its way forward early and creates a messy, ragged pace.
scenarios.body: A horse operating outside its mapped position fights for an early berth, disrupting the early rhythm and creating pockets of interference two to three out where the field narrows; horses with patient jockeys, clean jumping ability through traffic, and proven stamina who can find a gap late are best placed to exploit the resulting disorder.

watchPoints.text: Ghaiyya sets tempo alone — watch whether Rossa Ryan elects to roll along or crawl, as the pace she sets will determine whether this becomes a staying test or a false-run sprint that exposes every hold-up horse.|

Positional warfare in the first half-mile: Kirchner, Manxman, Small Fry, In The Breeze and Valedictory all want the same air behind Ghaiyya — a fierce scrimmage for the rail between the two-mile marker and the turn could cause interference affecting the race result.|

Manxman must be treated with great caution given 351 days off the track; if he blows up fitness-wise turning for home on this stiff York finish, James Doyle's mount could become an obstacle for horses attempting to come through on the inner.|

The redistributed group — Shrimp Shady, Boatswain, Kilmeaden, Fireblade, Mountain Road and Ride The Thunder — will all be racing out of role; watch for any of them making a forward move two to three out, as six horses suddenly producing an unplanned challenge could create a wall of traffic across the track.|

Valedictory's blinkers are on for the first time today — watch how she jumps off in the stalls, as William Buick on a headgear debutant over this marathon trip on good ground could mean an unusually sharp early break that alters the entire race shape.|

races.name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow

runners_data.comment: Naana's Shadow arrives here in sparkling form, a winner last time out and successful in four of her last six starts, with experience of today's distance and going in her favour; the 135 lb burden and draw 15 are the only notes of caution, but her recent record makes her the clear selection.

runners_data.name: Poatan
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose 67-day absence is the key query, but David Egan's positive booking for George Scott's yard suggests the horse is ready; acts on Good ground and has placed in this grade — will need a clean run through a congested field.
runners_data.comment: Poatan shaped with real promise when winning three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before; back-to-back thirds since show he retains form, though 67 days off and a stiff 132 lb ask are the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Revival Power
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but has run poorly on recent starts (0/0/W in last four attempts), suggesting the bold early pitch may flatter to deceive; Tim Easterby's barn is firing (T14:5/84) but the form decline is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Revival Power won at this trip and on this going five starts back, and her rating of 99 heads the field — but two unplaced efforts in a row are the concern she must overcome.

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning just three days after a run, which raises questions about recovery and freshness; has placed at this level but the back-to-back scheduling and no wins from 9 Good-ground runs is a red flag at this level.
runners_data.comment: Baker Blue arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second three starts back, showing consistent presence without always converting; the quick three-day turnaround and 127 lb from stall 11 are factors to weigh against his recent near-miss form.

runners_data.name: Schrodinger's Cat
runners_data.note: Consistently prominent racer with a superb 15-from-15 sim-going record; OR 94 and placed last time, Oliver Stammers takes over and Grant Tuer's yard had one winner from nine recently — high probability of getting a good position without being first to the front.
runners_data.comment: Schrodinger's Cat showed useful form with a second three starts back and a winner four starts back, but has disappointed in his last two outings; he has run over today's trip and going, returns fit enough on 20 days' rest, and 127 lb from stall nine are the key variables to weigh.

runners_data.name: Manatee Mehmas
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear noted and Daniel Tudhope riding; has won on Good ground at 5f and, at OR 92, holds realistic claims if the pace collapse brings the pack back to him — David O'Meara's yard is active.
runners_data.comment: Manatee Mehmas shaped well for third two starts back and has solid experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 97 marking him out as a leading player; the question is whether a disappointing eighth three starts back signals any vulnerability under a big weight.

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose last win came over 6f on soft, returned off 61 days; acts on Good at 5f and Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking — the layoff could mean he comes back cherry-ripe, but fitness must be proven on return.
runners_data.comment: Black Star Boy returns after 61 days off, and while he showed his best with a win three starts back, he has been unplaced on his latest outing and is unranked ninth of nineteen, making him a each-way proposition at best from stall one carrying 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Miss Yechance
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a tidy record across Good ground and a capable young apprentice claim of 3lb; at OR 90 this is competitive but K.R. Burke's yard placed six winners from 27 recently — worth respect in a prominent spot if the scrimmage ahead creates room.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner six starts back, Miss Yechance has experience over today's trip and returns on a sharp 20-day turnaround, but a seventh two starts back highlights some inconsistency that may limit her prospects from stall 7 off 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Tricky Tel
runners_data.note: Prominent type with three wins this term and has placed at 5f Good repeatedly; Hugo Palmer's yard is selective (T14:1/24) but the horse's record suggests it finds a way into contention and could benefit if the top of the market burns out.
runners_data.comment: Tricky Tel shaped well enough when runner-up last time out, and he has experience over today's trip and going, but the stable is struggling badly of late (1/24 in the last 14 days) and, drawn in stall 19 carrying 122 lb, he faces a stiff ask off a rating of 89.

runners_data.name: Zain Primus
runners_data.note: Has won three of three career starts on Tapeta/Standard — all of them — and this Good turf 5f is completely unexplored territory; John Butler's yard is busy (T14:7/27) but the massive going and surface question mark demands caution.
runners_data.comment: Zain Primus arrives on a 92-day absence and, despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts, our figures rank him 17th of 19, making him very hard to fancy; he has run over today's trip and a trainer striking at 26% is the one crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: Second last time at OR 86 but form before that is patchy; headgear noted (v=visor), zero wins from 8 Good-ground attempts, and Burke's second string after Miss Yechance — difficult to trust in a wide-open competitive race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Stargazed has nonetheless shown a placed effort two starts back and returns on familiar distance and going after a 25-day break, though she faces a stiff ask from stall ten carrying 119 lb with her form otherwise inconsistent.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse that won on Good at 5f twice and has a positive recent record; ran just three days ago which is concerning, but the pattern of Ian Williams placing this horse to run quickly again may signal it thrives with racing — needs luck in running from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures and beaten last time out and the time before, One And Gone faces a stiff task back just three days later, though he has winning form in recent starts and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Old Is Gold
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose OR 84 and recent mediocre form (830-60) suggest limited claims; with more prominent horses than positions available, Andrew Balding's runner is likely to find itself in a less comfortable midfield berth than ideal — the style compromise diminishes its prospects.

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but unplaced last three starts and without a turf Good win in this campaign; Joanna Mason takes the ride and the OR has drifted to 84 — the pace battle with three rival front-runners makes survival to the line unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Showed a third three starts back before a below-par latest outing, and her two wins in her last six starts suggest ability worth respecting; experience over today's trip and going helps, though her unplaced effort 20 days ago is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Underwriter
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse tagged as fading in finish — a pattern that makes a tough 19-runner, fast-pace scenario even more problematic; Luke Morris is experienced but the horse's tendency to stop running late makes it a speculative each-way play at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with unplaced efforts dominating a largely uninspiring recent profile, Underwriter is hard to fancy at a rating of 84 ranked well down the field, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 25-day break.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with a very strong sim-going record (11/14 on Good, 2W6P); Cam Hardie and Michael Dods have placed this horse to show up in this kind of race — if the pace is truly brutal, it has the profile to close into the places.
runners_data.comment: Mighty Magnus returns after 19 days off with distance and going experience in his favour, but a fifth last time out and just one win in his last six starts suggest he is more likely to fill a midfield berth than threaten at the finish, despite third two starts back keeping some hope alive.

runners_data.name: Dolos Dream
runners_data.note: Front-runner with two wins from 6 Good-ground runs; Silvestre De Sousa is a marquee booking and Ivan Furtado's horse is versatile enough to sit just behind the leaders if outpaced early — the De Sousa appointment is the sharpest positive angle in this race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, Dolos Dream is hard to fancy at the weights from stall 16, though she does arrive on the back of a second last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, with a win three starts back offering some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a poor record at 5f on Good (0W3P) and generally low-finishing runs in the last five; Tim Easterby second string and the 16-day turnaround does not obviously flatter — hard to make a case in this company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Boston Dan has little recent form to recommend him, and ranked 14 of 19 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; a fourth two starts back offers faint encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but that is about the extent of his claims.

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with one win on Standard (AW) at 5f but no turf wins from Good-ground attempts; Connor Planas (5lb claim) helps the weight, but the lack of Good-turf form and OR 79 makes this a long-shot to make an impact.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Call Margot has been largely out of the picture in her last two starts after a second three runs back, and her recent form makes her hard to fancy; she has run over today's distance and going, and 20 days since her last outing suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Revival Power, Baker Blue, Shes Got A Brother, and Dolos Dream all want to lead in a 19-runner, 5f York handicap — this race will ignite from the gates and burn at a relentless gallop that has little chance of easing. The front end will be congested immediately, likely creating scrimmaging and position-jostling in the first furlong before the field sorts itself, meaning the genuine pace-setters will burn themselves out defending ground rather than controlling tempo. With 8 of 19 wanting prominent positions, traffic will stack up dangerously from the 2-furlong pole as the hot early fractions take their toll on the leaders, compressing the field and bringing closers into play off the home turn. This shape unequivocally favours hold-up horses and late finishers able to pick through a tiring, congested pack — true front-runners and early-prominent types face maximum attrition, and the pace is simply too hot and too contested for any leader to dominate. Old Is Gold is a natural prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield because there are more front-running and prominent types than this race shape can physically accommodate; Revival Power and Baker Blue are the horses most likely to actually secure lead positions ahead of the wider prominent pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the confirmed leaders set a lung-bursting early clip and burn each other out, leaving the hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Four or more horses contest the lead aggressively, ensuring fractions are fierce and the field strings out before halfway; from the 2f pole, the hold-up horses find a clear run through the fading pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sits Just Off Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent racer secures a ground-saving position just behind the blistering leaders and outstays them in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The horse sits third or fourth tracking the suicidal pace, conserves energy while the leaders burn, and asserts near the line on fresh legs; Naana's Shadow and Schrodinger's Cat have the course form and prominent profiles to execute this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Leader Steals A March
scenarios.trigger: If a single front-runner clears the early scrimmage and establishes a clear lead by the 3f pole, dictating a more measured gallop.
scenarios.body: With rivals scrapping for position behind, a horse like Dolos Dream or Revival Power could slot into front uncontested and set a pace just sustainable enough to hold on; this is less likely given the number of rivals wanting the same position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Midfield Winner
scenarios.trigger: If congestion at 2-3 out creates a tight, bunched finish where a midfield horse threads through in the final stride.
scenarios.body: A messy 19-runner race with a packed prominent group can produce a wall of horses entering the final furlong, and a midfield runner who avoids the worst of the interference gets a clear passage at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Revival Power, Baker Blue, and Shes Got A Brother will all attempt to lead from the gates — monitor the first 2 furlongs for a fierce pace battle that could cause interference and unbalance the field.
With 8 of 19 runners wanting prominent positions, a wall of horses will converge between the 2f and 3f poles — any horse on the wide outside or trapped on the rail faces serious traffic danger.

One And Gone runs just three days after its previous start — watch the market closely; if it drifts in the betting, fatigue from the quick turnaround is a real concern in a pressured 5f sprint.

Dolos Dream's booking of Silvestre De Sousa into a relatively lightly weighted front-runner represents a notable trainer/jockey upgrade — if the pace softens even marginally, De Sousa's tactical awareness could make this horse more dangerous than its OR suggests.
