runners_data.name: Ruler's Pride
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in smart form (won last two), James Doyle booking is significant, three-from-three on Good ground and steps up to 6f where the extra distance may help; sits just behind the lead scrimmage and must avoid the early congestion.|
runners_data.comment: Ruler's Pride won three starts back but has since disappointed with an unplaced run and a seventh, so the current form is patchy; he has run over today's trip and comes here fresh on 21 days' rest, though carrying 135 lb from stall 8 is no help.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: Consistent and in excellent form with three wins from her last three, all on Good going at 5f-6f; Hector Crouch rides, and the step to 6f York on a flat, galloping track looks well-suited — the strong pace could play directly into her hands as a horse who races prominently but settles well.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Sprite has won three of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and she brings both distance and going experience into this. The 134 lb burden is a stiff ask against 21 rivals, though 18 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Crystal Queen
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a 63-day absence to overcome, Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) takes the ride; three-from-three on Good ground and her last two runs show a clear pattern of finishing well — the strong pace here is exactly what she needs, though the layoff introduces a fitness question.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and second three starts back, Crystal Queen brings solid recent form to this contest; she has run over today's trip and, while 63 days off the track is a query, the profile looks sound enough to give her a chance at 131 lb from stall 22.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this William Haggas-trained horse who is three-from-three on Good, with headgear (tongue-tie) fitted; two disappointing runs before winning last time suggest she can be inconsistent, and a wide draw or traffic trouble in a field of 22 would be problematic for a horse who wants to race prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has been well held in his two most recent outings, and at 131 lb from stall 11 he faces a stiff task; has run over today's trip and going before, though our rating of 87 leaves him needing to find significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking for the Ben Haslam yard is the headline angle; races prominently and has placed at 6f on Good twice, making this trip his optimum — the prominent position could be difficult to achieve cleanly in the first furlong with so many rivals wanting the same ground.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and finished second last time out, so Dubai Champion arrives in decent nick after 19 days; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 129 lb from stall 20 and a field of 22 make this a stiff test.

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged for fading in finishes, with Colin Keane aboard; wears a hood and has faded in two of his last three runs, which is a clear concern in a race where stamina will be thoroughly tested — needs to travel and finish in a way his record suggests he may not.|
runners_data.comment: Savage Mariner catches the eye on his second finish three starts back, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives with relevant experience; the concern is a trainer operating at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Persian Spring
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a win over 6f on Good ground; four-from-four on Good going makes the surface conditions ideal, and Richard Hannon has three runners in this race which suggests stable confidence — the strong pace setting up a late run suits his profile.|
runners_data.comment: Persian Spring won three starts back and arrives here fit on a 19-day turnaround, bringing distance and going experience that sharpens his claims; two unplaced runs since are the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will attempt to lead in a race with two direct rivals for the lead; Good-ground record is limited (two-from-four), and a three-way pace battle risks doing all the donkey work — only viable if he controls a moderate version of the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Glory won three starts back and was third four starts back, giving him recent placed form to point to, and he has run over today's trip before; carrying 128 lb from stall 16 is the main watch factor.

runners_data.name: Underdog
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win at 5f on Good, Saffie Osborne up; last run was a disappointing 10th at this trip on Good, and Richard Spencer's stable runs at a low recent rate — needs to find form after a 33-day break and that last run gives little confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Underdog returns after 33 days off with a win in his last four starts, and has run over today's trip and going, but two unplaced efforts sandwich that fifth, and carrying 127 lb from stall 17 makes this a tough ask for a midfield contender.

runners_data.name: Jumeirah Storm
runners_data.note: Ran three times over 6f on Good, winning once and placing twice — a very consistent record at this exact trip and going; Neil Callan takes the ride for William Knight and the horse has a hood (headgear:p), prominent style suits sitting just off what will be a fierce early pace.|

runners_data.name: Peaceful Warrior
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just two career runs, both on Good over 6f and both in the money (1W1P); Jamie Spencer partners for Kevin Ryan, a canny booking, and the 40-day break is a minor query, but the course, distance, and going tick every box for a horse with clear potential.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures and representing a trainer who has sent out just one winner from 22 runners in the last fortnight, Peaceful Warrior is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Elevating
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago which demands attention — stamina for the strong-pace 6f is plausible given his 6f form, but the quick turnaround for a two-year-old in a 22-runner field is a significant physical query; Joe Leavy up for Richard Hannon, and his form includes a win over 5f on Good.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but a well-beaten fifth last time out, and five days between runs leaves fitness a minor question; she has run over today's trip and her 126 lb burden from stall 18 gives the handicapper no margin for error.

runners_data.name: Towelontheterrace
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners who must fight for the lead with Sovereign Glory and Henley On Thames; Jason Hart rides for Jennie Candlish, who is in good 14-day form (4/10), and won over this course and distance on Good — but sharing the pace duel likely ends his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Towelontheterrace won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing he can compete at this level, though a fourth last time out tempers expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, and 125 lb from stall 13 is the key query.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Andrew Balding in a horse rated 83 with unknown true style (U); wears a hood, and four runs all on Good are encouraging, but a placing record of just one second in four runs and a 7th last time are modest — Murphy's positional intelligence is the key asset here.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last four starts, The Dancing Pirate does bring a second two runs back alongside distance and going experience, and 19 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the seventh last time out is the obvious concern, though draw two and a rating of 89 offer mild encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rlasthope
runners_data.note: Won last time on Standard (AW) but only one run on Good ground and has not shown that form on this surface convincingly; Ray Dawson rides for a small yard (T14: 1/8), and the class step into a 22-runner competitive handicap is a significant test — AW win may flatter.|
runners_data.comment: Rlasthope showed his best when winning last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but he has been placed three times in his last four starts without winning those, and carrying 122 lb from stall 15 may not make life easier.

runners_data.name: Henley On Thames
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner who won on Good over 6f last time; David Egan partners for Kevin Philippart De Foy and the horse is four-from-four on Good — the pace duel with Sovereign Glory and Towelontheterrace is the central question, and only a clear lead without a full burning contest gives him a chance.|

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a win over 6f on Good; Oliver Carmichael (7lb claim) is an inexperienced rider in a 22-runner field which introduces a tactical risk — the horse has place form on Good at this trip but needs a clean passage, and the apprentice may struggle to find it in a congested field.|

runners_data.name: Bear Lee

runners_data.name: Brandenburg

runners_data.comment: Ranked 18th of 22 on our figures, Brandenburg is hard to fancy despite a smart recent sequence that includes wins last time and three starts back, with a runner-up finish sandwiched in between; he has run over today's trip and returns after 33 days, but the ratings profile makes him a tough sell.

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Glory, Towelontheterrace, and Henley On Thames are all confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field, guaranteeing a fierce early battle for the lead that will set a strong, sustained gallop from the outset on this flat 6f York track. With nine of 22 runners wanting prominent positions, the opening two furlongs will see significant jostling and crowding, creating real traffic danger in the middle stages as the field fans out between the 2f and 3f markers. The strong pace will test stamina fully and will burn off horses who over-race or get trapped wide, favouring those able to settle just off the frenzy and produce a clean late run. This race shape firmly suits hold-up and late-finishing profiles that can track the speed at a sensible distance, pick a clean passage, and pounce as the lead horses tie up; prominent types who can sit second or third without being consumed in the early scrimmage also have claims. Brandenburg is a natural prominent type and Sue's Last Chance a genuine hold-up horse — both are redistributed on the map because the field holds more front-runners and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, with Sovereign Glory, Towelontheterrace, and Henley On Thames most likely to actually secure the lead positions ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fire off a genuine fast gallop and burn each other out by halfway, leaving late-runners to sweep past the weakening pace setters.
scenarios.body: The strong early fractions will have the front three tying up inside the final furlong, opening a clear run for hold-up horses tracking in fourth to seventh who have settled without using energy early; on Good ground at York's straight 6f, there is enough room to weave through a tiring field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sits Off Scorching Pace
scenarios.trigger: If a horse in fourth or fifth survives the prominent scrimmage, settles just behind the lead skirmish, and strikes once the front-runners burn.
scenarios.body: A compact second-row mover who races within herself in the early chaos will find the leaders at their most vulnerable inside the final furlong as the strong pace bites; this scenario rewards a horse with strong Good-ground form and the tactical nous to pick the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three confirmed front-runners manages to steal a decisive march on the pack and controls a strong but not suicidal pace, dictating throughout.
scenarios.body: Sovereign Glory or Towelontheterrace could use rail position and a clear lead to set a rhythm they control rather than a full-on duel, and on Good ground York's straight track does not punish a front-runner who gets a clean passage; a horse that wins from in front here must have the class and stamina to sustain to the line despite the attritional gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Creates Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage causes widespread interference between 2f and 3f out, splitting the field and leaving a midfield horse to emerge through the mayhem unscathed.
scenarios.body: In a field of 22 with nine wanting prominent, traffic pile-ups in the middle of the race can create chaotic openings that a well-positioned midfield runner with a sharp turn of foot can exploit in the final furlong; this is the least predictable shape because it depends on others' misfortune rather than genuine race-pace dynamics.
